subject: How to parse expressions to guides?

messages.author: c74e427e565f8938
messages.subject: How to parse expressions to guides?
parts:
How can I parse the context of a grouping/colour variable to the guide?
I.e. I would like to use the following syntax:
ggplot(data,aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_line(aes(colour=guide))
where the variable 'guide' is a part of the data.frame 'data' and contains strings like "q[1] == 0.03" and so on.
Is there a parse=TRUE option somewhere for guides() or the like?

messages.author: d588a03e58ea7e7f
messages.subject: Re: How to parse expressions to guides?

On 6/16/2014 6:34 AM, Torben Tvedebrink wrote:
> How can I parse the context of a grouping/colour variable to the guide?
> I.e. I would like to use the following syntax:
> ggplot(data,aes(x=x,y=y)) + geom_line(aes(colour=guide))
> where the variable 'guide' is a part of the data.frame 'data' and contains
> strings like "q[1] == 0.03" and so on.
> Is there a parse=TRUE option somewhere for guides() or the like?

There is not a parse option for guide labels, but you can get the same
effect with a custom label function

First some dummy data


DF <- data.frame(x=1:10, y=1:10,
guide=rep(c("q[1] == 0.03", "q[2] == 0.45"), each=5))


Now the custom label function

guideparse <- function(x) parse(text=x)


And an example in use


ggplot(DF, aes(x=x, y=y)) +
geom_line(aes(colour=guide)) +
scale_colour_discrete(labels=guideparse)
